## The readings behind that JSON

Measurement round for the parking decision on this PR. ⛔ Nothing here was repaired, nothing was
pushed, no label or draft state was touched. Angle-bracket placeholders in quoted tool output are
respelled as CAPS words, because the comment sanitizer eats short tag-shaped fragments.

### 1. The red, reproduced

Worktree at head `73b3ba07b` merged locally with `origin/main` `0c2eb5eee` — merge commit
`45cb11f5c`, conflict-free, **local only, never pushed** (`ls-remote` still shows the branch at
`73b3ba07b`). Exit captured before any pipe:

```
node scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs > log 2>&1; EXIT=$?   →   EXIT=1
```

```

    reconstruction does not match the pinned upstream blob

      actual : 4ef9be2cccee54737f9e40e591e70c9ba1c77116b6faa5baaf4f42ed7256fc76
    Every declared divergence still applied cleanly, so the difference is OUTSIDE all of them —
    either this copy was edited without declaring it, or upstream moved.
✗ check-upstream-port-parity: 1 of 11 ported file(s) drifted. ⛔ Do not edit the pinned digest by
  hand to clear this — that baselines the drift the gate exists to catch.
```

The other ten entries print `✓ byte-identical … modulo N declared divergence(s)`. Re-run as the
last act: unchanged, `EXIT=1`.

**The instrument is healthy, so the red is a finding and not a broken gauge.** `--self-test` exits
0 with 66 cases. The ported sweeper's own `--self-test` on the merged state exits **0 with 1579
cases**, so this PR's change survives today's `main` intact.

### 2. What the gate says it is for, in its own words

> the ported objectstack tooling in this tree is a PINNED copy, and drift from the pin is RED.

> The pin … carries, per ported file, the upstream ref it was taken from, the SHA-256 of that
> upstream blob, and the DECLARED DIVERGENCES as exact text pairs. Verification runs backwards …
> Byte equality is the assertion, so there is no "close enough" reading and no heuristic to tune.

Two satisfying acts, and one forbidden one. The re-sync:

> `--resync` applies the declared divergences FORWARD onto the new upstream text, writes the ported
> file, and rewrites THAT ENTRY's ref and digest … It is the only supported way to move the pin,
> because the alternative — editing a digest by hand until the gate goes green — is
> indistinguishable from baselining the drift it exists to catch.

And the divergence, deliberately fenced:

> ## The divergences are a checklist, not a licence
>
> Every entry carries a `why`. An adaptation nobody can justify in one sentence is drift that was
> written down rather than drift that was decided, and the self-test refuses a pin whose entries
> lack one. The set is meant to SHRINK.

That last paragraph is what makes this a routing question rather than a repair.

### 3. Sizing the divergence — with a control, and the answer is unambiguous

Extraction control first: the SHA-256 of the objectstack blob at the pinned ref `bf10debd5` equals
the pin's `upstreamSha256` (`449a0aec…`) **exactly**, so the thing being compared is the pinned
thing.

| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| ported@merge-base vs upstream@pinned | **11** | +12 / −149 |
| ported@PR-head vs upstream@pinned | **20** | +39 / −232 |
| ported@merge-base vs ported@PR-head (this PR alone) | **9** | +83 / −27 |
| upstream@pinned vs upstream@objectstack-main | **185** | +23715 / −505 |

11 + 9 = 20. Zero-controls taken in the same command: an identity diff gives 0 hunks at exit 0, and
the same command on a real pair gives 11 hunks at exit 1.

**There is no pre-existing drift — none at all.** The gate is green at this branch's merge-base
`b67b53bc0` (exit 0) *and* on today's `origin/main` `0c2eb5eee` (exit 0), both printing
`11 ported file(s) match`. Reversing the 11 declared pairs on the base copy reproduces `449a0aec…`

command over `scripts/` shows 119 files changed, so it can see movement).

Reversing the same 11 pairs on the **PR head** gives `4ef9be2c…` — the exact `actual` the gate

byte-identical (sha256 `2ab06013…`) to this PR's own change to the file.

⇒ **100% of the drift is this PR's, and it lies entirely outside every declared region.**

Sizes for scale: upstream@pinned 12,966 lines · ported@base 13,103 · ported@head 13,159 ·
upstream@objectstack-main **36,176**.

### 4. Two things the PR body does not have

**The divergence reds a second required check.** The port-parity wiring test carries a case titled
*"and the tree itself is at parity right now"*, which shells the gate out with `execFileSync` and
therefore throws when the tree is drifted. Replicated locally on the merged state: **THREW, child
status 1**; the same shape against the merge-base worktree **RETURNED**. Check-run controls agree —
`Test (shard 1/4)` is `success` at this branch's own base `b67b53bc0` and `success` on today's
`main`, and `failure` on the head. So `Lint` and `Test (shard 1/4)` are one cause, not two.

⚠️ The shard failure's *identity* is inferred, not read: the Actions job-log endpoint redirects to
blob storage the egress proxy denies (`connect_rejected`), and I ran no vitest. Recorded as NOT
MEASURED with that reason.

**The re-sync route is priced at about half its cost, and is currently refused outright.** The body
quotes objectstack `32a32143` at 24,443 lines. objectstack `main` is now `1739f7187` at **36,176**
lines. More decisively — applying the declared divergences forward onto that text:

| upstream text | anchors still applying |
| :--- | :--- |
| `bf10debd5`, the pinned ref *(control)* | **11 of 11** — forward rewrite reproduces the base copy's 13,103 lines exactly |
| `1739f7187`, objectstack main today | **6 of 11** |

The five that have vanished: `summary-unread-branch`, `closed-window-resolver`,
`closed-window-fetch-gate`, `summary-disabled-beats-floor`, `closed-window-self-test` — the whole
objectui-only disabled-closed-reader and page-window family. A `--resync` today is **refused**, not
merely large. It would also **destroy this PR's fix**, since it writes the port from upstream text
plus forward divergences and carries no undeclared local edit.

One cost this route does *not* carry: this port is **not** governed surface — `resyncWriteVerdict`
returns write true / governed false for it (control: a `.claude` hook returns write false /
governed true) — so no `--rewrite-governed-file` and no content-neutrality proof.

### 5. Route A is mechanically proven, computed without touching the tree

The residual is **14 contiguous changed regions**, and all 14 bare upstream sides are **already
unique anchors** — 0 need widening (control: a known-unique string counts 1, a known-repeated one
counts 953). Synthesizing 14 pairs and reversing 11 + 14 on the head reproduces `449a0aec…`:
route A **would go green**. Control: the existing 11 alone stay red. Price: the declared set for
this file goes **11 → 25 entries (+127%)** and **158 → 241** ported snippet lines (+53%).

Computed entirely in scratchpad memory. ⛔ No pin, no port and no tracked file was written.

### 6. Fence

`objectstack-ai/objectstack` was **read only** — `git show` of two blobs, nothing else. No branch,
no edit, no push, no card there. The upstream copy still carries `NO MECHANISM THAT WILL EVER
RELEASE IT` **4 times** and `NO SCHEDULED RELEASER` **0 times** (control: `H22` hits 239 times in
the same file, so the grep is live). Filing the upstream card is the maintainer's call and outside
this seat.

The routing call is the maintainer's. The recommendation in the JSON above — **C, with A-expiry as
the fallback and B filed separately** — is a recommendation, not an action taken.
